title: Agentic Trading with Robinhood
author: lil_pepper09
selftext:
I’ve been exploring whether an AI agent could scan the market, identify options setups, and help manage trades through Robinhood.

Has anyone here built something like this that has actually been profitable with live money, not just in backtesting?

I’d be interested to know:

* What tools, models, and market data are you using?
* What strategies have worked best, such as swings, spreads, or 0DTE?
* How do you handle position sizing, stop losses, and risk limits? (Robhood doesn't allow bracketed orders.
* How long has it been running profitably after slippage and losses?
* Are there any GitHub builds or frameworks worth checking out?

I’m especially interested in smaller-account options strategies with trades lasting a few days to two weeks.. I’d just like to hear from people who have built something legitimate and tested it with real trades.

comments.author: Rare_Inflation3178
comments.body:
We’ve built something similar, although not around Robinhood specifically.  
Here’s what we’ve learned:  
**Models:** LLMs are useful for research and filtering setups, but we still rely on structured market data and quantitative signals for actual decisions.  
**Strategies:** Swing trades and systematic spreads have been much more robust than 0DTE. The shorter the holding period, the more execution quality dominates.  
**Risk:** Position sizing and predefined risk limits matter much more than the model. We don’t let the agent decide leverage on its own.  
**Live performance:** We don’t trust backtests alone. Every strategy has to survive forward testing with realistic slippage before touching meaningful capital.  
**Frameworks:** There are plenty of open-source agent frameworks, but honestly the hard part isn’t orchestration. It’s building a reliable validation pipeline around the strategy.  
We actually ended up building a lot of those validation tools ourselves because we couldn’t find anything that tested ideas the way we wanted before going live.

replies.author: pig_newton1
replies.body: Thanks for the insights. Can you give any guidance on what stack you’re using ? Like where you getting your market data from and what platform you trading on?

replies.author: Rare_Inflation3178
replies.body:
Sure. We mainly work with crypto and equities.  
For equities we use Massive, and for crypto we primarily use Hyperliquid, Binance, and Deribit.  
We store everything in DuckDB/Parquet so we can replay markets and run realistic forward tests.  
We built our own execution and validation layer because we found that's actually much harder than the agent itself.  
Curious what market you're mainly trading?

comments.author: MStellarQuest
comments.body: You will find that Claude fable and other agents are not very smart when it comes to setting this up. You have to have quite a bit experience and what to look for to train your models. You can build the trading agent and a research agent for back testing. As much as I try to train the agent and build with Claude it’s still a pain in my ass for fully autonomous. There is no magic indicator. Closest I got has been programming in options data for autonomous lines with GEX research and imported data. This has been the closest to a lot of the action so far with my software auto updating where the dealer and whale flows are going to collect premium.
